oil_life_monitor: The Oil Control System (OCS) calculates engine oil and filter change intervals based on driving conditions. Under light conditions (freeway driving, city driving on flat/moderate hills, no towing or heavy loads, no extended engine idling), the OCS displays a normal change interval. Under extreme conditions (repeated short trips under 5 miles, repeated short trips under 10 miles in below-freezing temperatures, hot weather stop-and-go traffic, extensive idling/low-speed driving, car-top carrier use, frequent braking or mountainous driving, sustained high-speed driving), the OCS triggers an early change indicator. If the oil replacement indicator is displayed, change the engine oil and filter within two weeks or less than 500 miles (800 km). If the OCS resets prematurely or becomes inoperative, change the oil within six months or 5,000 miles (8,000 km) from the last oil change.
severe_conditions: Repeated short trips of less than 5 miles (8 km)
Repeated short trips of less than 10 miles (16 km) with outside temperatures remaining below freezing
Operating in hot weather in stop-and-go 'rush hour' traffic
Extensive idling and/or low speed driving for long distances, such as police, taxi or door-to-door delivery use
Driving on rough, muddy or salt spread roads
Towing a trailer, using a camper or using a car-top carrier
extraction_caveats:
1. The maintenance schedule pages (602–613) are formatted as milestone columns (every 5,000 miles) rather than a simple interval table; intervals were reconstructed by identifying the repeating pattern across milestones.
2. Engine oil & filter: The standard schedule shows replacement every 10,000 miles/12 months, but the OCS may shorten this. The severe schedule also shows oil replacement at every 10,000-mile milestone.
3. Brake fluid: Standard schedule shows replacement at 20k, 40k, 60k, 80k, 100k, 110k miles (every 20,000 miles/24 months). Severe schedule shows replacement at every interval (5k through 110k). Reported as 20,000-mile/24-month repeat interval.
4. In-cabin microfilter and Intelligent Key battery: First replacement at 15,000 miles/18 months, then every 30,000 miles/36 months.
5. Drive belts inspection: First appears at 40,000 miles in the schedule, then every 10,000 miles thereafter; marked with * (recommended, not required for emission warranty).
6. EVAP vapor lines & fuel lines: Marked with * (recommended, not required for emission warranty). Appears at 20k, 40k, 60k, 80k, 100k miles.
7. Engine valve clearance: No specific mileage interval given in the schedule pages provided; described as 'inspect only if valve noise increases.'
8. Coupling oil and Transfer fluid capacities are not listed in the provided pages.
9. ATF capacity is not listed in the provided pages (shown as '—' in the fluids table on page 617).
10. Differential gear oil capacity is not listed in the provided pages (shown as '—' in the fluids table on page 617).
11. Engine coolant capacity: Both 'with tow package' (11.9 L / 3-1/8 gal) and 'without tow package' (11.6 L / 3-1/8 gal) values round to the same US gallon figure as printed.
12. The schedule explicitly covers up to 120,000 miles/96 months (standard) and 144 months (per page 602), with instruction to continue at same intervals thereafter.
13. Automatic transmission fluid replacement at 90,000 miles is based on miles only (not months), per footnote (6).
14. Spark plug replacement at 105,000 miles is based on miles only, per footnote (6). Replace earlier if plug gap exceeds 0.053 in (1.35 mm).
15. Engine coolant first replacement at 105,000 miles or 84 months; subsequent replacements every 75,000 miles or 60 months. Marked with * (recommended, not required for emission warranty).
16. Brake pads/rotors, exhaust system, drive shaft boots, propeller shaft, and steering gear/linkage appear at every severe interval (every 5,000 miles/6 months) starting at 5k, and at every standard interval starting at 10k.
17. Differential gear oil, coupling oil, and transfer fluid inspections appear at every standard 10,000-mile interval starting at 10k.
